root_cause.text: svm_copy_lbrs() unconditionally marks the destination VMCB dirty (VMCB_LBR), which is architecturally incorrect when copying to vmcb12 (the L1 guest VMCB) during nested SVM VMexit, because clearing the clean bit in vmcb12 is not defined by the architecture and can cause undefined behavior.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "svm_copy_lbrs() always marks VMCB_LBR dirty in the destination VMCB. However, nested_svm_vmexit() uses it to copy LBRs to vmcb12, and clearing clean bits in vmcb12 is not architecturally defined." The patch removes the vmcb_mark_dirty() call from svm_copy_lbrs() and adds it only at the callers that target vmcb01 or vmcb02, not vmcb12.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional dirty marking inside svm_copy_lbrs() is the direct root cause: it marks the destination VMCB dirty even when the destination is vmcb12 (L1 guest VMCB), which architecturally should not have its clean bit cleared during nested VMexit.
This function call invokes svm_copy_lbrs with vmcb12 as the destination during nested VMexit, triggering the unconditional dirty marking and thus the vulnerability.
This condition determines whether vmcb12 is used as the destination for svm_copy_lbrs. It is part of the vulnerable path because it selects the problematic call when LBR virtualization is enabled.
This else branch call uses vmcb01 as destination, which is architecturally correct, but its presence demonstrates the dichotomy and underscores that only the vmcb12 call is problematic.

This call in another context (not vmcb12) is not directly vulnerable but shows that svm_copy_lbrs is used with other destinations, making the unconditional dirty marking potentially problematic in other scenarios as well.
